candidates.name: Quiet Catastrophes — forgotten local & industrial disasters
candidates.niche: Narrative documentaries on forgotten/under-covered historical disasters: mining collapses, maritime sinkings, structural failures, fires — especially long-tail and non-Anglosphere events the big channel (Fascinating Horror) has not covered
candidates.format: 15-30 min narrated documentary: archival photos, animated maps/diagrams of the failure mechanism, human-written research-heavy script, AI or self-recorded narration
candidates.why_now: The niche leader Fascinating Horror (1.44M subs, 315M views — YouTube API) proves a large ceiling, and brand-new channels are still breaking in during 2025-2026: DisastersUncovered (created 2024-12-22) pulled 478k views on a 28-min Aberfan video published 2026-04-10. Two separate channels each got 100k-250k views on near-identical Tenerife disaster videos in May-June 2026, showing demand exceeds supply even on covered topics.

demand_evidence.finding: DisastersUncovered 'The Aberfan Disaster' (pub 2026-04-10, 28m10s): 478,348 views — from a channel with only 26.6k subs, i.e. ~18x sub-to-view outperformance

demand_evidence.title: YouTube Data API videos.list
demand_evidence.finding: Two different channels' 87-min Tenerife disaster docs got 248k views (The Aviation Channel, 12.1k subs, pub 2026-05-20) and 108k views (On The Move, pub 2026-06-10) within weeks — duplicate topics still get absorbed, indicating unmet demand

competitor_scan.notes: Niche leader, created 2019-01-17, 315M views, 453 videos. Covers mostly famous Anglosphere disasters — long tail left open
ATTAINABILITY PROOF: created 2024-12-22 (~19 months old), 3.76M views across 64 videos, 478k-view breakout in April 2026
Created 2023-12-20, 2.42M views, 253 videos — aviation-disaster vertical works even at micro scale
Hyperlocal (one Colorado mining town), 950k total views on 40 videos — shows even single-locality disaster history draws views

candidates.monetization_notes: History/documentary RPM benchmarks $4-10 with Tier-1 audience (per fluxnote.io/toolbil search snippets, reliability C). Disaster content skews US/UK/AU viewers. Fascinating Horror's Patreon + memberships model transfers directly. Inference: some advertiser-sensitivity on tragedy content; mitigated by the proven calm/non-graphic house style.
candidates.production_complexity: Low-moderate: public-domain archival photos, simple map/diagram animation, one narration track. Research (newspaper archives, accident reports) is the main labor — which is also the originality moat. Fully faceless, solo-feasible at 1 video/week.
candidates.originality_defense: Each video is original research synthesis from accident-investigation reports and newspaper archives with custom failure diagrams — not compilation footage. The long-tail/non-Anglosphere angle means most topics have no existing English-language video at all.
candidates.risks: Fascinating Horror owns the famous events — must go long-tail. Tragedy content carries demonetization pockets (inference). Somber tone limits crossover virality. Some archival imagery rights require care.

candidates.name: How Nations Break — economic & demographic collapse history
candidates.niche: Economic history explainers on national collapse: hyperinflations, sovereign defaults, land-reform disasters, demographic implosions, deindustrialization — case-study format (one country/crisis per video)
candidates.format: 15-25 min explainer: charts, animated maps, archival footage stills, human-written analytical script over AI narration; Fall-of-Nations-style causal chain storytelling
candidates.why_now: Macro-anxiety in 2026 is pulling huge numbers to historical economic collapse content, and the two fastest risers in the lane are both under 2 years old: Fall of Nations (created 2024-10-31) is at 204k subs/43.5M views, and Dr. Jonathan Tam (created 2025-08-28) hit 109k subs/13.3M views in under 11 months with a 6M-view video on Japan's demographic collapse. Mainstream interest confirmed by Big Think's Eric Cline 1177 BC interview ranking in top economic-history results for 2026.

demand_evidence.title: YouTube Data API videos.list
demand_evidence.finding: Dr. Jonathan Tam 'How Japan Finally Made It Impossible to Make Babies' (pub 2026-03-12, 20m28s): 5,996,229 views — on a channel less than 1 year old

demand_evidence.finding: Fall of Nations Zimbabwe land-reform economic collapse video (pub 2026-05-02, 18m34s): 1,978,165 views in ~10 weeks

demand_evidence.finding: Third-party page documents the channel's rapid rise ('untold stories of collapsing empires... economic disasters') and notes its production model is plausibly AI-hybrid — confirming the niche is winnable with AI-assisted solo production

competitor_scan.notes: ATTAINABILITY PROOF: created 2024-10-31 (~20 months), 43.47M views, 285 videos. Faceless, likely AI-assisted
ATTAINABILITY PROOF: created 2025-08-28 (<11 months), 13.33M views on 107 videos, one 6M-view breakout on demographic-economic history
Adjacent finance-explainer incumbent surfacing in the same searches (subs not pulled via API this session); competes on present-day economics, leaving deep-history cases open
'How To Destroy An Economy' ranked top-10 for the niche query in 2026 (subs not pulled via API this session)

candidates.monetization_notes: Best RPM of the four lanes: finance-adjacent content benchmarks $8-22 RPM vs $1-5 entertainment (outlierkit/tastyedits search snippets, reliability C). Economic-history titles attract finance advertisers plus sponsors (brokerages, news apps). Inference: RPM likely lands between pure history ($4-10) and pure finance.
candidates.production_complexity: Moderate: needs genuine economic-data research (World Bank, historical GDP/inflation series), chart design, and careful causal argumentation. Visuals are charts + maps + archival stills — solo-feasible. Higher scripting skill bar than the disaster lane.
candidates.originality_defense: Value is in analytical synthesis — assembling data series, academic economic-history literature, and primary reporting into an original causal argument per case. No compilation footage; every chart is generated from sourced data.
candidates.risks: Politically charged topics (Zimbabwe, immigration, demographics) invite comment wars and mislabeling risk; accuracy failures are reputationally fatal in this genre. AI-slop competitors are multiplying in exactly this lane (factually.co flags Fall of Nations itself as possibly AI) — differentiation must come from verifiable sourcing. Some topic overlap with big geopolitics channels.

candidates.name: You Wake Up In... — sensory everyday-life history beyond medieval Europe
candidates.niche: Second-person / immersive 'what it was actually like' daily-life history (smells, food, hygiene, work, sleep) — applying the proven medieval-Europe format to underserved settings: Edo Japan, Roman insulae, Bronze Age cities, Gilded Age tenements, 1970s USSR
candidates.format: 10-20 min immersive narration with period-accurate AI-generated imagery and ambient sound design; optional companion POV Shorts (JokeLore model) as a growth engine
candidates.why_now: The everyday-life format is exploding across every size tier in 2026 and the newest entrant proof is extreme: George's History was created 2025-12-25 and already has a 947k-view video ('1348: No Showers, No Toilet Paper — Life in the Middle Ages'). Medieval Mindset (created 2024-03) is at 207k subs with a 2.79M-view May 2026 video. Nearly all of this supply clusters on medieval Europe, leaving other eras/civilizations open with identical viewer psychology.

candidates.monetization_notes: History RPM $4-10 Tier-1 (search-snippet benchmarks, reliability C); broad all-ages appeal helps volume. Shorts arm monetizes poorly (~$0.01-0.06 RPM per snippet data) but drives subs to long-form. Merch/book-list affiliate potential. Inference: slightly lower RPM than economic history but higher viral ceiling.
candidates.production_complexity: Low-moderate: script research from social-history books and primary sources, AI imagery generation with period-accuracy checking, sound design. The main craft risk is visual consistency. Solo-feasible at 1-2 long-form/week plus Shorts.
candidates.originality_defense: Original narrative scripts grounded in academic social history (diet, labor, medicine, hygiene scholarship) — the sensory-detail specificity IS the research product. No third-party footage. Differentiates from medieval-clustered incumbents by owning non-European and modern-era settings they don't cover.
candidates.risks: The medieval slice is already crowded — must commit to underserved eras where search volume is unproven (labeled inference). AI-imagery historical inaccuracy draws credibility attacks from history communities. Format is easily copied; moat is script quality and era breadth.

candidates.name: The Accurate Sleep Historian — rigorous long-form history for sleep
candidates.niche: 2-3 hour calm, quiet-narration 'history to fall asleep to' videos (everyday routines, slow chronicles) — positioned explicitly as the human-researched, accurate alternative in a niche currently flooded with error-ridden AI slop
candidates.format: 2-3 hr low-stimulation narrated long-form: soft human-directed narration, minimal slow visuals, human-written primary-source-based scripts; chapters for repeat listening
candidates.why_now: Demand is documented and enormous — 404 Media reported AI 'boring history' sleep videos flooding YouTube with individual 2-hour videos at 2.3M views — and brand-new entrants still break in: Sleepy History with Oliver was created 2026-01-31 and already has 24.9k subs, 2.2M views, and a 409k-view 2h34m video. The same reporting shows the supply is dominated by glitchy AI slop 'drowning out real history,' which is precisely the quality gap a rigorous human-scripted channel exploits.

competitor_scan.channel: Boring History For Sleep / Sleepless Historian / Dreamoria
competitor_scan.notes: Named by 404 Media as the AI-slop incumbents (stats not pulled via API this session) — quality gap is the opening

candidates.monetization_notes: Watch-time economics are the draw: 2-3 hr videos allow many mid-rolls, and sleep viewers replay nightly (repeat views compounding on a small catalog — see Historically's 4.5M views/video average, API data). History RPM $4-10 benchmarks apply (snippet data, reliability C). Inference: effective RPM may be reduced if viewers are asleep/screen-off (ad skip behavior unverifiable).
candidates.production_complexity: Moderate: each video needs a 15-25k word accurate script — the biggest labor item — but visuals are minimal (slow pans, ambient scenes), making the edit trivially solo-feasible. Cadence of 1 long video/week is realistic with AI-assisted drafting + human research verification.
candidates.originality_defense: This is the niche where originality is the entire pitch: incumbents are documented AI slop with fabrication and voice glitches (404 Media). Differentiation = human-verified primary-source scripts, citations in description, consistent narrator persona, and 'actually accurate' branding. No reused footage; fully original narration and text.
candidates.risks: HIGHEST-RISK candidate: association with a slop-flooded niche invites YouTube 'inauthentic/mass-produced content' policy scrutiny (inference — enforcement behavior unverified this session); discovery competition against high-volume AI farms; audience may not distinguish quality pre-click, so packaging must carry the accuracy positioning. Platform could algorithmically demote the whole genre.
